subject: Data shelf-life and customer-scoped retention variance request
messages:
From: Matt Reynolds <matt.reynolds@clearbridgehealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Question about data shelf-life for session logs

Hi Naomi,

We're prepping for our SOC 2 audit and the auditor flagged a gap: they expect a 24-month forensic retention window for conversation/session logs used in clinical triage workflows. I understand Redwood's standard tenant session/log TTL is 30 days (and ephemeral inference logs are pruned earlier), but ClearBridge needs a customer-scoped variance for a subset of tenants for compliance.

Two quick asks: can you confirm whether Redwood supports a tenant-specific retention extension to 730 days today, and if not, what the proposed remediation and evidence would look like for SOC 2 reviewers (exportable attestation, delivery format, chain-of-custody notes)? Also, will enabling a longer retention path change how logs are stored (S3 vs hot cache) or the encryption/KMS envelope used?

We're trying to decide whether to request a formal retention carveout in the audit and need material we can share with our auditors by end of next week.

Thanks,
Matt Reynolds
Director, Security & Compliance
ClearBridge Health

---

P.S. If helpful I can share the auditor's exact control wording — attaching a short note in a follow-up if needed.

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Matt Reynolds <matt.reynolds@clearbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question about data shelf-life for session logs

Hi Matt — thanks for the clear ask and context. We can support a tenant-scoped retention extension, but the approach and deliverables vary depending on exactly which artefacts need to be preserved (raw session transcripts, inference traces, KV cache snapshots, and/or access logs).

I attached a short summary (log-retention-summary.pdf) that outlines our standard preservation tiers and the current operational path for longer-term retention. High-level notes:
- Customer-scoped retention extension is possible via an archival pipeline that moves data to encrypted, WORM-style S3 buckets with explainable access controls.
- We can produce an export package (CSV + redacted JSON) and a signed attestation that shows chain-of-custody and retention policy at the time of export.
- Enabling the extension will add storage and egress costs; we'll provide a sizing estimate after we see a sample data profile.

Next steps I propose:
1) Jordan (CC'd) will draft a recommended evidence pack and timeline.
2) Irene (CC'd from Legal/Compliance) will confirm whether the attestation language meets Redwood's standard SOC 2 templates or if we need Legal signoff.
3) Matt, if you can share the auditor wording and an approximate volume (daily session count / avg size) we can give a firm quote and target delivery date.

Would you prefer a short call tomorrow or is email fine?

Best,

Subject: Re: Question about data shelf-life for session logs

Thanks Naomi and Matt — I pulled together an operational proposal and attached two internal playbooks that show how we implement tenant-scoped retention and the preservation controls we apply. Summary below for auditors:

Operational proposal (summary):
- Scope: tenant-scoped archival of session transcripts, inference metadata (model id + generation timestamps), and access logs. KV cache and ephemeral GPU artifacts are not preserved unless specifically flagged.
- Retention target: configurable up to 1095 days (3 years) but we recommend 730 days to balance cost and audit needs.
- Storage: data lands in a dedicated Redwood S3 account bucket per-customer with enforced bucket policy (deny-delete unless legal hold lifted), server-side encryption with customer-managed KMS (if requested), and MFA-delete enabled for the retention lifecycle.
- Evidence & attestation: we can produce a time-stamped export bundle, MD5 checksums, export audit log showing who requested the export, and a signed Redwood compliance attestation which references the CAIQ/SIG control mappings.
- Timeline: for an initial sample export (<= 200GB) we can deliver evidence + attestation within 7 business days after scoping; full-scale archival provisioning will be scheduled based on capacity and will typically take 2-4 weeks.

Cost note: extended retention is billed as a combination of archival storage + export/egress events; we will provide a detailed cost estimate after reviewing volume.

Attachments: tenant-retention-playbook.docx, s3-preservation-guidelines.pdf

Irene — for compliance signoff on attestation language I suggest we reuse our standard SOC 2 export attestation and add one paragraph specific to the customer-scoped variance. Matt — if you can share the auditor wording and an example of the session size distribution we will start scoping.

Jordan Blake
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference

Naomi / Jordan — this looks good, thanks for the quick turn. A few follow-ups from our auditor:

1) Encryption: can you confirm whether tenant-scoped archival supports customer-managed KMS keys? Our legal requires a KMS where ClearBridge retains control of the key lifecycle for long-term retention.
2) Attestation: can we see a redline/sample attestation now? The auditor wants to review the exact language referencing CAIQ controls.
3) Cost: rough ballpark on storage for 730-day retention for the sample tenant (we have ~120GB/day of session data currently; retention applies only to clinical triage subset ~15% of traffic).

If you can provide a sample attestation and a ballpark cost by EOD Thursday we can decide whether to request the formal carveout for the SOC 2 scope. Also — what operational triggers would cause us to lift a retention hold (court order, legal notice, internal incident)?
